definition: Governance structures that include affected communities in decision-making about AI development and deployment. Emphasizes standing, representation, and veto power for those who bear consequences rather than delegating authority to technical experts or market forces.
rationale_for_coinage: Skeptics insist governance must include the governed — not just experts and industry. Safetyists default to expert-led governance; accelerationists prefer industry self-regulation or market governance. The bare term 'governance' conceals who governs and on whose authority.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Governance oversight is expert-led institutional constraint; participatory governance is community-inclusive decision-making.
Adaptive governance is AI-augmented dynamic governance; participatory governance prioritizes human community authority.

contested_aspects: Whether meaningful participation scales beyond local contexts
How to balance technical expertise with community authority
Whether participation slows governance to the point of ineffectiveness
